en.title: Street Fighter's New Trailer: Ken and Ryu Finally Settle Their Differences
en.summary: A brand-new trailer for the upcoming Street Fighter movie has dropped, showing fan-favorite rivals Ken and Ryu putting aside their differences. The footage promises a thrilling blend of iconic martial arts action and playful self-awareness.
en.body:
The world of fighting games is gearing up for another cinematic showdown as a new trailer for the **Street Fighter** movie arrives, and it’s already got fans talking. This latest glimpse offers a tantalizing look at iconic characters **Ryu** and **Ken**, two of the franchise's most enduring rivals, seemingly working together. After years of competitive clashes and philosophical differences, seeing them united against a common threat hints at a narrative that respects the series' core dynamics while forging a new path.

The trailer showcases the film's commitment to capturing the kinetic energy of the games. The fight choreography looks sharp and impactful, promising bone-crunching blows and flashy special moves that fans have come to expect. But beyond the pure action, there's a noticeable sense of fun and a wink to the audience. The film appears to embrace the inherent theatricality of its arcade origins, balancing serious martial arts sequences with a knowing nod to its cartoonish roots. This tonal tightrope walk, if executed well, could be the key to making this adaptation a standout in the often-treacherous landscape of video game movies.

## A Tournament of Legends, and a Familiar Threat

The overarching plot, as suggested by the trailer and existing lore, revolves around the nefarious **M. Bison** summoning the world's greatest fighters to a tournament. This classic setup provides the perfect stage for a sprawling cast of characters to clash. While **Ryu** and **Ken** take center stage, the inclusion of characters like **Guile** and **Akuma**, portrayed by real-life wrestling stars **Cody Rhodes** and **Roman Reigns** respectively, adds an intriguing layer of crossover appeal. The trailer also teases potential standout moments for **Jason Momoa**, **Eric Andre**, and **David Dastmalchian**, the latter tasked with the unenviable but exciting challenge of filling the shoes of the legendary **Raul Julia**.

## What the Fans Are Seeing

For long-time fans, this trailer is a potent cocktail of nostalgia and anticipation. The visual design, the character interactions, and the promise of epic fight scenes all tap into the deep well of affection for the **Street Fighter** universe. The decision to seemingly pair **Ryu** and **Ken** early on might raise eyebrows for purists, but it also opens up exciting storytelling possibilities, allowing for deeper exploration of their bond and shared history. The film's apparent willingness to blend serious action with a touch of playful absurdity has generated considerable buzz, with many hoping this adaptation will finally capture the *spirit* of the games in a way previous attempts have struggled to achieve.

## What's Next

The **Street Fighter** movie is slated for release on October 16, 2026. With this trailer now out in the wild, expect further promotional material in the coming months that will undoubtedly reveal more about the assembled cast and the epic battles to come.

content_raw: Some trailers—like, for instance, a Grand Theft Auto 6 trailer —are meant to be consumed slowly and carefully, dissected and analyzed, until every last bit of information is wrung out of them. Others are about nothing more than kicking back and enjoying the fun. The new promo for the upcoming Street Fighter film is definitely one of the latter, and I'm really starting to think that as videogame movies go, this might be a good one. We're not talking about great cinema here, and the overarching story, well, it's Street Fighter: M. Bison has invited the world's greatest fighters to a tournament for unknown but certainly nefarious purposes, and it's up to the gang to put a stop to it. (Image credit: Paramount Pictures) I can't put my finger on exactly why, but this image is very funny. But it looks like the movie might just strike the right balance between taking itself seriously—the bits of fight scenes look very Street Fighter but also have pleasingly bone-crunching impact—and not seriously at all, with a full understanding that it's built entirely around a cartoonish arcade game rooted in the mid-1980s. There's a very pro wrestling vibe to it, really, which is appropriate given that two of the sport's biggest stars—Cody Rhodes and Roman Reigns—play prominent roles in the film, as Guile and Akuma. Rhodes in particular has a couple of choice moments in this video, even though the focus is clearly on Ryu, Ken, and Chun-Li, but I expect (or, more accurately, hope) the full film will deliver scene stealing moments from Jason Momoa, Eric Andre, and of course David Dastmalchian, one of the few men who might have the juice to live up to Raul Julia's magnificent " It was Tuesday ." I'm reading a lot into a single trailer, so take it for what it's worth: It's a fast, flashy video with good action, catchy music, and a funny stinger. Whether or not that adds up to a good movie remains to be seen, but at this point I'm feeling pretty hopeful about it.
